Q: How to properly use colorScheme in Flutter? A:

If the default color palette provided by colorScheme is not enough for you or you too are not satisfied with the pallet generated for the seed color, you should read about ThemeExtension for ThemeData. Not that this might require you to overwrite lerp method which for me was complex for some cases as a beginner. As an alternative, you might also try a pub.dev package flex_color_scheme.

Q: Nextcloud Office - built-in CODE server - restrict to localhost? A:

The built-in CODE server cannot be restricted to localhost via configuration. Security must be handled at the network level (firewall, Docker networking, etc.).

Q: Why does jOOQ ignore non-nullability when using forcedType? A:

Check out the documentation page regarding annotation generation. There's a nullableAnnotationOnWriteOnlyNullableTypes flag.

A column that contains a DEFAULT expression is "write only nullable," i.e. it is possible to leave a null value when inserting the record, even if it is never null when reading the record.

Q: Dockerized Symfony app debug in VSCode - 9003 port occupied A:

Just comment out ports in users service - it helps

Q: SkAndroidCodec::NewFromStream returned null A:

The issue is:

  • not cookies,
  • not HTTPS,
  • not certificates,
  • and not Skia itself;

the real problem is that you are opening the connection and decoding the image manually, but still returning a URL, so Google Maps fetches the tile again and Skia ends up decoding non-image data (WMS error/HTML) or an already consumed response, which results in SkAndroidCodec::NewFromStream returned null. Removing cookies on the server " fixes " it only because the server stops returning error pages, not because cookies are handled correctly !

Using HostnameVerifier, SSL setup, closing streams, or try-with-resources does not fix the logic bug...

A TileProvider must do one thing only :

  • either return a valid WMS tile URL and let Google Maps handle networking, or implement a full custom TileProvider that downloads the tile and returns new Tile(256, 256, byte[])

Mixing both approaches will always break, even if everything else looks correct.

Q: Assign colors of geom_lines with multiple legends by group in a nested facet_wrap A:

You can use scale_color_manual with an appropriately defined named color vector:

library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggh4x)
library(legendry)

# Named color vector
pal_color <- df0 |>
  distinct(
    site, analyzer, color_analyzer
  ) |>
  unite(
    "site_analyzer", site, analyzer,
    sep = ":."
  ) |> 
  deframe()
# Looks like color assignment was wrong
pal_color["SY:.Y2_B"] <- "blue"
pal_color["SY:.Y1_C "] <- "dodgerblue1"

# disordered colors
df0 |>
  filter(analyte == select_analyte) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year_month, y = cv, group = analyzer)) +
  ggtitle(paste0(select_analyte)) +
  facet_wrap2(
    vars(qc, site),
    ncol = 3,
    drop = FALSE,
    scales = "free_y",
    strip = strip_background
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(mult = 0.05)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = breaks_pretty(n = 4)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = pal_color
  ) +
  geom_line(
    # Add the subgroup name and the seperator = "." used to split into groups
    aes(color = paste0(site, ":.", analyzer)),
    linewidth = 1.3
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = expression("cv")) +
  theme(
    plot.margin = unit(c(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 0.5), "cm"), # trbl
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", vjust = 1),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, vjust = 1),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "grey10", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(0.6, "cm"),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(0.3, "cm"),
    strip.background = element_rect(color = "black", linetype = "solid"),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 13, color = "black"),
    strip.text.y = element_text(size = 13, color = "black", angle = -90),
    axis.title.x = element_text(vjust = -0.5, size = 13),
    axis.title.y = element_text(vjust = 4.8, size = 13),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      margin = margin(b = 0.1),
      hjust = 1.12, vjust = 1.05, colour = "black", size = 10, angle = 60
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      margin = margin(l = -5, r = 2.5),
      colour = "black", size = 10
    ),
    legend.margin = margin(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.direction = "vertical"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend_group(
    key = key_group_split(sep = "\\."),
    override.aes = list(linewidth = 4),
    nrow = 1,
    title = NULL
  )) +
  theme(
    legendry.legend.subtitle.position = "left",
    legendry.group.spacing = unit(0, "cm"),
    legendry.legend.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 12 # or rel(1)
    )
  )

Q: Is PyArrow Append Columns an In-Place Operation? A:

No, append_column is not an in-place operation, it does not cause double memory usage either.
In PyArrow, pa.Table objects are immutable. When you run table.append_column(...), PyArrow creates a new Table object.
